subject: Azure private plan: data certification, SLA amendment & procurement checklist
messages:
From: Amy Lopez <amy.lopez@terrahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: data certification + SLA amendment for Azure private plan

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the TerraHealth team is excited to move forward with an Azure Private Plan. Before procurement finalizes the PO we have two asks that are blocking legal/infra sign-off:

1) Data certification: we need a short doc confirming what logs and telemetry Redwood will persist, retention windows for telemetry and user query artifacts, and controls around customer-managed KMS for tokenization. Attached is a template (Azure_Cert_Reqs.xlsx) from our security team with the exact items they need.

2) SLA amendment: our legal team requires a narrow amendment to the standard SLA for private plans that includes an uptime SLO, credits formula, and a data-residency breach notice clause. Can you share a proposed redline?

Procurement would also like an estimated onboarding timeline and any standard gating artifacts (SOC2 evidence, runbook access). Can you loop in whoever owns the marketplace commercial docs?

Appreciate it — happy to set a call if that’s faster.

Best,
Amy Lopez
Head of Cloud Procurement, TerraHealth
amy.lopez@terrahealth.com

Attachments: Azure_Cert_Reqs.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lopez <amy.lopez@terrahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-07T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: data certification + SLA amendment for Azure private plan

Amy — thanks for the clear list. I attached a first-pass SOW and a draft SLA amendment (Redwood_Proposed_SLA_Amendment.docx) that addresses uptime credits and notification windows. High level:

- Telemetry and logs: we retain control-plane logs for 180 days by default; customer query payloads are not retained beyond 30 days unless explicitly opted-in for debugging. We support customer-managed KMS for workspace-level encryption (details in the SOW).
- SLA: proposed 99.9% uptime for production endpoints with tiered credits; incident notification within 2 hours for SEV1s and 24 hours for SEV2s (we can tighten to 1 hour if required by contract).
- Onboarding: typical timeline is 4–6 weeks once PO is executed (legal review + provisioning + certing).

Marissa — tagging you for legal redlines; Lauren — can you confirm if finance can absorb the standard onboarding credits request below?

Next step: if these items look reasonable, we can circulate redlines and then route to DocuSign for the procurement PO.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Attachments: TerraHealth_SOW_v3.pdf, Redwood_Proposed_SLA_Amendment.docx
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Amy Lopez <amy.lopez@terrahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-08T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: data certification + SLA amendment for Azure private plan

Amy/Karthik — looping in our commercial counsel. Quick legal notes after an initial pass on the SLA redline:

- Data purge: TerraHealth needs a firm 30-day maximum for customer data deletion requests. Karthik’s note about 30 days for query payloads is fine; we should add a contractual clause that commit to deletion timelines and provide a verification mechanism (audit log).
- KMS: we'll accept customer-managed KMS but need an indemnity carveout for keys managed by the customer; propose a limited liability cap tied to the monthly contract value.
- Credits: prefer a caps-and-floor approach. We'll propose a 10% monthly credit cap; see draft redlines in PDF comment.

Amy, could legal confirm whether the verification mechanism (simple certification of deletion + telemetry snapshot) is sufficient? If they require an independent attestation, that will add time.

I’ve also flagged the DocuSign flow and will prepare a clean signature-ready SOW once comments are resolved.

-M
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quoted message:
> On Mon, Dec 7, 2026 at 11:03 AM karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> > Amy — thanks for the clear list. I attached a first-pass SOW and a draft SLA amendment...
From: Amy Lopez <amy.lopez@terrahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@terrahealth.com
Date: 2026-12-08T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: data certification + SLA amendment for Azure private plan

Marissa — thanks for the quick review. A couple of clarifications from TerraHealth legal/procurement:

- Deletion verification: an exportable audit log and a signed certificate from Redwood’s security team will be sufficient; we do not require a third-party attestation at this stage.
- KMS indemnity: acceptable with a limited liability cap — procurement will propose cap language during final redline.
- Credits cap: procurement asks for a 15% monthly credit cap (TerraHealth rarely experiences incidents but prefers a slightly higher safety margin). Is Redwood flexible on moving from 10% -> 15%?

Procurement also asked whether Redwood can provide the SOC2 report and a short runbook excerpt for our platform engineers to review. If you can upload those internally to the HubSpot deal or provide a secure link, that would speed things up.

Amy

Attachments: none
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-09T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: data certification + SLA amendment for Azure private plan — onboarding credits

Looping in re: onboarding credits & co-sell note. Team — TerraHealth is in the co-sell pilot for Q1; they requested two items that impact commercial math:

1) Small onboarding credit (one-time) to offset engineering integration time — TerraHealth asked for $5k.
2) Slightly expanded credits cap request to 15% monthly (Amy’s note).

If legal is comfortable with the 15% cap and Marissa can adjust the redline accordingly, I endorse approving the $5k onboarding credit for the pilot. This will help close the PO faster and aligns with our co-sell incentive program. I’ll note it in the deal record (HubSpot link in metadata).

Happy to discuss if anyone thinks we should escalate to Revenue Ops.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lopez <amy.lopez@terrahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-10T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: data certification + SLA amendment for Azure private plan

Amy — great, thanks for the confirmations. Plan of record:

1) Marissa will deliver a redlined SLA with the 15% monthly credit cap and the 30-day deletion verification clause (audit log + signed security certificate).
2) We will accept customer-managed KMS with a limited indemnity cap tied to the first 3 months of contract value — Marissa will include the language.
3) Redwood will provide SOC2 and a runbook excerpt via the HubSpot deal link (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/TH-2026-042) by EOD 12/11.
4) Redwood will apply a one-time $5,000 onboarding credit for TerraHealth as part of the Q1 co-sell pilot.

If that matches TerraHealth’s expectations I’ll ask our contracts team to prep the DocuSign packet and route the SOW for signature. Amy — please confirm and I’ll start the DocuSign flow.

Thanks everyone — moving to action.

Karthik
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
